data.headline: Treasury yields fall, led by the long end
data.summary: On November 25 the ten- and thirty-year Treasury yields both fell six basis points, to 4.85% and 5.24%. The two-year yield declined two basis points to 4.61%.

bull.text: The ten-year yield fell from 4.91% to 4.85%, lowering the benchmark for some longer-term borrowing costs.

watch.text: The ten-year spread over the two-year narrowed from 28 to 24 basis points. The thirty-year spread over the ten-year stayed at 39 basis points.

limitations: Treasury reports constant-maturity par yields. The market and ETF outcomes are measured separately using verified session prices.
